evidence_added: Caps(gpu_hours, cloud_usd) optional (None = unenforced); Attempt.finish records them; usage() sums; exhausted()/begin() refuse with typed CapExhausted.cap before the START row (REFUSED row written, as for existing caps); est_gpu_hours/est_cloud_usd on begin() refuse a run that would pass the cap
inventory emits gpu_micro_hours/cloud_micro_usd integers only on rows that recorded them; old ledgers read unchanged

red_observed.detail: tests written after the first implementation draft; RED observed by stashing ledger.py and running the new class (1 failure, 6 errors), then restored

known_escapes: First draft treated the real contract's gpu_hours 0 / cloud_usd 0 as 'used >= limit' and refused every CPU-only run (29 s2_bundle errors); caught by the slice suite and fixed: refusal needs non-zero spend or a declared estimate past the limit. Test test_zero_cap_is_no_paid_compute_not_no_runs pins it
Callers that do not pass est_* or record spend on finish() are not metered; the ledger only counts what it is told
One test run was auto-backgrounded by the harness (timeout); no run_in_background was requested
notes: Field decisions: refusal writes a REFUSED row like existing caps (no START); inventory units are micro-hours / micro-USD integers because canonical bytes refuse floats; check order launches, cpu, bytes, gpu, cloud.
